title: Peperomia ( Peperomia spp.) Indoor Plant Care and Growing Guide

paragraphs.heading: Factsheet | HGIC 1567 | Published: Jan 15, 2026 | Print
paragraphs.text: Sunlight: Bright indirect light Watering: Let the soil dry out between waterings Best Soil: Well-drained potting soil mix Care Tips: Be careful not to overwater Blooming: Blooms are insignificant

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Plant Overview, Origin, and Natural Habitat
paragraphs.text: Watermelon peperomia ( Peperomia argyraea ) features silvery striped foliage and reddish stems. Millie W. Davenport, ©2024 HGIC, Clemson Extension

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Plant Overview, Origin, and Natural Habitat
paragraphs.text: Peperomia are native to Central and South America. In their native habitat, they live in the forest’s understory.

paragraphs.heading: Ornamental Features of Peperomia
paragraphs.text: Peperomia Flowers: The flower spikes are produced when the plants are actively growing in the spring and summer. They are considered unattractive and are said to resemble a rat’s tail. Removing them enables the plant to focus its energy on leaf production.

paragraphs.heading: Best Soil for Peperomia
paragraphs.text: Plant peperomia in a well-drained houseplant or cactus potting mix. Since it does not need to be repotted every year, it can remain in the same pot for several years.

paragraphs.heading: Best Soil for Peperomia
paragraphs.text: Peperomia should be planted in a slightly larger pot than the grower’s pot.

paragraphs.heading: Light Needs for Peperomia
paragraphs.text: Place peperomia where it will receive indirect light from east or south-facing windows. It can even tolerate somewhat low light near a large north-facing window.

paragraphs.heading: Light Needs for Peperomia
paragraphs.text: If it gets direct sun, the leaves may scorch.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Peperomia Plants
paragraphs.text: Peperomia prefers to dry out between waterings. If it is overwatered, it will drop its leaves.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Peperomia Plants
paragraphs.text: It is best to water and let it drain before placing it back in the saucer. It will benefit from a humidifier in the winter.

paragraphs.heading: Fertilizing Peperomia
paragraphs.text: Fertilize peperomia only when it is actively growing in the spring and summer.

paragraphs.heading: Fertilizing Peperomia
paragraphs.text: A low-strength liquid fertilizer can be used occasionally during the growing season. Another option is to use a slow-release granular fertilizer once per year.

paragraphs.heading: Fertilizing Peperomia
paragraphs.text: For more information on houseplant fertilization and care, see HGIC 1450, Indoor Plants-Cleaning, Fertilizing, Containers, and Light Requirements .

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Cold Tolerance and Protection Tips
paragraphs.text: Plants can be taken outdoors for the summer after temperatures are consistently 60°F or higher at night, typically in May. Plants should be placed in deep shade to acclimate.

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Cold Tolerance and Protection Tips
paragraphs.text: Leave them in a bright, but shady spot for the summer, where they do not receive direct sunlight.

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Cold Tolerance and Protection Tips
paragraphs.text: For more information on moving plants outdoors in spring, see HGIC 1454, Moving Houseplants Indoors and Outdoors .

paragraphs.heading: Watermelon Peperomia ( Peperomia argyraea )
paragraphs.text: Watermelon peperomia is easily distinguished by its striped foliage resembling a watermelon rind. It is a small, bushy plant that grows to a height of 8 inches.

paragraphs.heading: Baby Rubber Plant ( Peperomia obtusifolia )
paragraphs.text: The baby rubber plant has rounded, thick, succulent-like leaves that are either variegated or solid green. It has low water needs, and it is very easy to grow.

paragraphs.heading: Baby Rubber Plant ( Peperomia obtusifolia )
paragraphs.text: With its variegated heart-shaped leaves, the ripple peperomia ( Peperomia caperata ) makes a great office window plant. Barbara H. Smith, ©2024 HGIC, Clemson Extension

paragraphs.heading: Baby Rubber Plant ( Peperomia obtusifolia )
paragraphs.text: Raindrop Plant ( Peperomia polybotrya ) The raindrop plant has shiny, green leaves that are shaped like teardrops. Overall, the plant grows to 12 inches tall and wide.

paragraphs.heading: Baby Rubber Plant ( Peperomia obtusifolia )
paragraphs.text: It is often mistaken for the Chinese money plant ( Pilea pepermioides ), but it is easier to grow.

paragraphs.heading: String of Turtles Peperomia ( Peperomia prostrata )
paragraphs.text: It is sensitive to being overwatered.

paragraphs.heading: How to Propagate Peperomia Plants
paragraphs.text: Stem Cuttings: a. Cut a three-to-five-inch piece of the stem from the parent plant. b. Remove the leaves on the lower third of the cutting. c. Dip the stem in rooting hormone, then insert it into potting soil or a rooting medium. d. Cover with clear plastic and place it in a location out of direct sunlight.

paragraphs.heading: How to Propagate Peperomia Plants
paragraphs.text: Leaf Cuttings: a. Remove a leaf with at least an inch of the petiole (leaf stem). b. Insert the leaf into a rooting medium. c. New plants will form at the base of the petiole. d. They can then be removed and potted. e. For more information on leaf cuttings, see

paragraphs.heading: How to Propagate Peperomia Plants
paragraphs.text: Water Propagation: Some species, such as the baby rubber plant ( Peperomia obtusifolia), are easily propagated in water. a. Take cuttings that are 4 to 6 inches long and remove the lower leaves. b. Cut just below a leaf node. c. Place the cutting in a small container where it will receive bright, indirect light. d. After roots and new leaves form, it can be potted.

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Disease Issues
paragraphs.text: Root Rot: This is caused by overwatering and is the most common disease of peperomia. After watering, drain the water from the pot before placing the pot back in its saucer. Allow plants to dry out between waterings.

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Disease Issues
paragraphs.text: Fungal Leaf Spots: Can be prevented by ensuring the leaves stay dry when the plant is watered.

paragraphs.heading: Peperomia Pet Safety
paragraphs.text: Most peperomia are considered safe for pets. Consult the ASPCA Poisonous Plants site for more information.
